title: Exploring Electronics
description: Electronics from first principles — voltage, current, resistance, and circuit design explained clearly. Real components, real numbers, no prior knowledge assumed.

items.title: Soldering
items.content_html: How soldering works: solder bonds only to clean, hot metal. Heating the parts, flux, choosing solder and temperature, judging a joint, desoldering, and fume and lead safety.

items.title: Bench Power Supplies
items.content_html: How a bench power supply works: an adjustable regulator with a current limit. CV and CC modes, the crossover, a safe first power-up, and reading the spec sheet.

items.title: SPI
items.content_html: How SPI works: two shift registers swapping bits on every clock, a chip-select wire instead of an address, clock modes, and reading an MCP3008 ADC from an Arduino.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: The Communication articles in reading order: serial between two devices, the I²C bus for many sensors on two wires, and fast SPI with a wire per device.

items.title: I²C
items.content_html: How the I²C bus lets an Arduino talk to many sensors on two wires: open-drain lines and pull-ups, a shared clock, 7-bit addresses, ACK, and reading an MCP9808.

items.title: Serial Communication
items.content_html: How serial (UART) works: one bit at a time on one wire, no clock, just an agreed baud rate. Framing, wiring TX to RX, voltage levels, and two-way Arduino serial.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: The Power articles in reading order: cells and batteries, then voltage regulators and the power supplies that turn a wall outlet into steady DC.

items.title: Voltage Regulators
items.content_html: How a voltage regulator holds a steady output: linear regulators and their heat, dropout, switching regulators, and the stages of a complete power supply.

items.title: Vacuum Tubes
items.content_html: How a vacuum tube works: a heated cathode, a positive plate, and a grid that controls the stream. Diodes and triodes, why tubes resemble FETs, and why they're still made.

items.title: Using a Multimeter
items.content_html: How a multimeter works: why the jacks matter more than the dial, what the fuse and CAT rating protect, auto-ranging and accuracy, and the habits that keep readings honest.

items.title: Voltage Dividers
items.content_html: How two resistors split a voltage, why the output collapses under load, and how to scale a 12 V battery down for an Arduino's analog pin safely.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: The fourteen Circuit Foundations articles in reading order: charge, voltage, current, resistance, Ohm's law, AC, magnetism, capacitors, and inductors, with real numbers.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: The Components articles in reading order: resistors, diodes and LEDs, transistors, vacuum tubes, temperature sensors, and the physical packages parts come in.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: The Microcontrollers articles in reading order: the Arduino board and its code, digital pins, blinking an LED, reading buttons and analog sensors, and staged output.

items.title: Overview
items.content_html: The bench equipment this site uses: breadboards, arduino-cli for programming an Arduino, the multimeter, the bench power supply, and soldering.

items.title: Inductors
items.content_html: How an inductor stores energy in a magnetic field and resists any change in current: the henry, what sets a coil's inductance, the L/R time constant, and why switching one off bites.

items.title: Transistors
items.content_html: How a transistor lets a tiny current or voltage control a large one: bipolar and field-effect transistors, switching a 12 V load from an Arduino pin, and amplifying.

items.title: Diodes and LEDs
items.content_html: How a diode lets current through one way only, why every LED colour has its own forward voltage, how to size an LED resistor properly, and what diodes do in real circuits.

items.title: Capacitors
items.content_html: How a capacitor stores charge between two plates, what a farad is, why it fills on an RC curve, and how a camera flash turns two AA cells into a 15 kW burst.

items.title: Resistor Types
items.content_html: What's inside carbon, metal-film, and wire-wound resistors, what a temperature coefficient means, and how potentiometers, rheostats, trimmers, and tapped resistors work.
